title: 02 Trigonometric functions: Visual Guide
outline: 1. From Triangle To Circle | one angle slider driving the unit circle, with the old right-triangle ratios (including csc, sec, cot) computed beside the new coordinates | setting the hypotenuse to 1 turns sine and cosine into the y and x coordinates of a point, which is the only definition that survives past 90 degrees

2. Radians Or Degrees | an angle slider in 15-degree steps and a radius slider, with the arc marked in whole radii and unrolled into a straight bar | a radian is the arc divided by the radius, so it does not change when the circle does, and every conversion is the one fact pi rad = 180 degrees

3. Special Angle Triangles | buttons for 0, pi/6, pi/4, pi/3 and pi/2 rebuilding the 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangles scaled to hypotenuse 1, plus a complementary-angle overlay | the exact values come from two familiar triangles, the short leg always faces the small angle, and pi/6 and pi/3 swap because sin(theta) = cos(90 - theta)

4. The Identity Holds | an angle slider showing cos squared and sin squared as two blocks of a bar that always totals exactly 1, plus worked completions of cos x = 5/13 and sin x = 3/5 | sin^2 + cos^2 = 1 is the unit-circle equation x^2 + y^2 = 1 renamed, so it gives a magnitude in every quadrant and the quadrant supplies the sign

5. Unwrapping The Curves | a point walked round the unit circle while the sin, cos or tan curve traces itself alongside, with the tangent asymptotes drawn | sine is the height and cosine the same wave started at its peak, both amplitude 1 and period 2pi, while tan is a ratio so it has asymptotes, period pi and no amplitude at all

6. Fit The Wave | four sliders over y = A sin(B(x - C)) + D with live amplitude, midline, period, phase shift and range, quiz-shaped presets, and a data strip fitting a Ferris wheel and a tide table | amplitude is |A| measured from the midline, the period is 2pi/|B| rather than B itself, subtracting C moves the graph right, and a delayed peak can only be the phase shift
